card.name: Punta
card.era: Garifuna pre-1797 St. Vincent · Modern Honduran-Belizean
card.tagline: The Garifuna people's signature dance — hips driving at impossible speed to garaon drum, the Afro-Indigenous Caribbean heartbeat.
card.profile: Punta is the foundational dance of the Garifuna people — the Afro-Indigenous Caribbean nation descended from West African and Carib-Arawak peoples who fled to St. Vincent before being forcibly resettled to Honduras's Bay Islands in 1797 by the British. Today the Garifuna communities of Honduras, Belize, Guatemala, and Nicaragua keep punta alive at every wake, wedding, and celebration. The dance is centred on rapid hip articulations and weight transfers (men and women dancing solo or facing partners) to the polyrhythmic beat of the garaon (large skin drum), often combined with shaker and turtle-shell percussion.
card.insight: In 2001, UNESCO proclaimed the Garifuna language and culture to be "a masterpiece of oral and intangible heritage of humanity", in recognition of the risk of an endangered status and loss of such an interesting culture.
